subject.title: Onboarding Wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup as a mandatory step

question: Should first-run onboarding/configure treat memory embedding setup as mandatory, prominently optional, or diagnostic-only, and what credential/probe UX should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but making embeddings mandatory can change first-run success, credential storage, provider cost, and daemon environment expectations, which are product and security-adjacent choices rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Prominent Optional Setup
options.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness path that configures existing memorySearch provider/model and SecretRef or API-key fields, then verifies with a probe or memory status guidance.

options.title: Mandatory Gate
options.body: Require users to configure embeddings or deliberately choose FTS-only before completing onboarding, maximizing recall readiness at the cost of first-run friction and provider dependency.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep onboarding lean and rely on doctor, status, and Crestodian repair guidance, accepting that some users may still miss memory readiness until later.

recommendation.title: Prominent Optional Setup
recommendation.body: Add a visible but skippable memory setup/readiness path that configures existing memorySearch provider/model and SecretRef or API-key fields, then verifies with a probe or memory status guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman is the current issue assignee and participated in the product-scope discussion on this exact report.
